cells.tense: Right now, you're the one seeing the pattern — and you know you're seeing it.
cells.verb: Reading what's actually there beneath what's being said.
cells.place: In the middle of not knowing how it'll go, moving anyway.
cells.ask: You're free to offer one feeling you haven't checked first — say the want before you've weighed it, and let what comes back be connection rather than a conclusion.
cells.core:
You're in the middle of something undecided and you can still see the shape of it. Not forcing the picture to finish itself — noticing what's actually there, letting the next step show up when it shows up. The clarity is real and it isn't brittle. It's the kind that can sit inside a question without needing to close it.

What you can do from here is let it reach someone. There's a pull in you toward what might be felt — yours and theirs — and following it isn't a loss of the clarity. It's what the clarity is for.
cells.sheetLine: You see the pattern without having to finish the picture.

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead of you there's a version where this all makes sense — and you're already living there.
cells.verb: Solving what hasn't happened yet, faster than it can arrive.
cells.place: Standing in a fog that hasn't lifted, refusing to move until it does.
cells.ask: You can hand one thing the structure it's asking for — a rule, a boundary, one clear line — and then let the thing organize itself around it, rather than forcing the whole shape into view. When it's in balance, what you understand is something people can walk on.
cells.core:
You're running the analysis ahead of the situation. Every unknown gets pre-solved, every ambiguous move gets mapped three steps out, and the mapping has started to replace the moving. You're not actually in the fog — you're above it, describing it, waiting for it to clear so you can finally walk. But it doesn't clear from up there. The pattern you keep reaching for only shows up once your feet are in it.

The instinct is good. It's just running without you in the room.
cells.sheetLine: You're solving the fog instead of walking through it.

cells.tense: You used to be able to see it — there's a version of you, back there, who could.
cells.verb: Holding the picture still, waiting to be sure before you read it.
cells.place: At the edge of something unclear, not stepping in.
cells.ask: You can put one half-formed thing in front of someone who'd get it — not to be judged, just to be walked alongside — and let the meaning of it come back to you through them. When it's in balance, what you understand becomes something you can hand to another person, alive and still moving.
cells.core:
The seeing is still in you. What's gone quiet is the willingness to trust it before it's complete. Somewhere back there, reading the situation wrong cost you something, and since then you've been waiting for enough light to see the whole road before you take a step. So the step doesn't happen. The pattern-recognition is idle, and the fog you're standing in isn't the situation's — it's the one you've been keeping yourself in until it's safe to move.

The capacity didn't leave. It just hasn't been asked.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped trusting what you see before it's finished.

cells.tense: You're already reading the room — and talking about it like it's reading itself.
cells.verb: Naming the pattern as if it were just how things are.
cells.place: Inside the uncertainty, calling it weather.
cells.ask: You can put one word on something you've felt about this — a pull, a lean, a preference — and let that be enough to go on. When it's in balance, what you see reaches another person as recognition instead of analysis — theirs and yours at once, neither swallowed up.
cells.core:
You're already doing the work. The pattern is being read, the shape is being named, the situation is being understood — and every time it comes up you describe it as if it just is that way, as if anyone in your seat would see the same thing. They wouldn't. You're the one cutting through it.

The seeing is yours. The credit for it has been going somewhere else — to the facts, to the situation, to how things obviously are. Nothing about the reading is wrong. Only the pen has been set down in a room you're still writing in.
cells.sheetLine: You're reading the situation and calling it the situation reading itself.
